dataDisclaimer: Fares checked against operator and agency sources on Oct. 31, 2026, and converted at Federal Reserve rates for Oct. 23, 2026 (nominal, not purchasing power parity).

nyc.name: New York City
nyc.monthlyNote: No monthly pass: average month at the $35 OMNY 7-day cap ($35 x 52 weeks / 12, our calculation)

london.name: London
london.busNote: £1.85 from Nov. 1, 2026 (was £1.75); Hopper transfer free for 1 hr
london.monthlyNote: Zone 1-2 monthly Travelcard (3.84 x the £44.70 7-day price)

paris.name: Paris
paris.singleRideNote: Métro-Train-RER ticket, any distance in the region (2026)
paris.fareSystem: Flat ticket price region-wide + monthly Navigo pass

tokyo.name: Tokyo
tokyo.singleRideNote: Tokyo Metro minimum fare, 1-6 km (¥178 with IC card); rises with distance
tokyo.busNote: Toei bus flat fare, cash or IC
tokyo.monthlyNote: No flat monthly pass: commuter passes are priced by route

seoul.name: Seoul
seoul.singleRideNote: Base fare with transit card, first 10 km (since June 28, 2025)
seoul.busNote: Blue (trunk) bus base fare with card (since Aug. 2023)
seoul.monthlyNote: Climate Pass (기후동행패스, since Sept. 1, 2026): spending above ₩62,000 a month is refunded. Replaced the Climate Card.

beijing.name: Beijing
beijing.singleRideNote: Base fare, first 6 km; rises with distance
beijing.busNote: ¥2 for first 10 km, half price with a Yikatong card
beijing.monthlyNote: No monthly pass; subway discounts of 20% after ¥100 and 50% after ¥150 spent in a month

shanghai.name: Shanghai
shanghai.singleRideNote: Base fare, first 6 km (a fare revision went to public hearing in Sept. 2026)

hongkong.name: Hong Kong
hongkong.singleRideNote: Lowest adult Octopus fare on MTR heavy rail; distance-based
hongkong.busNote: Varies by route and operator; not verified
hongkong.monthlyNote: No network-wide monthly pass: route-based Monthly Passes cost HK$430-675 (2024 prices; MTR fares frozen in 2025 and 2026)

exchangeRateNote: U.S. dollars per unit, Federal Reserve H.10 rates for Oct. 23, 2026 (FRED series DEXUSUK, DEXUSEU, DEXJPUS, DEXKOUS, DEXCHUS, DEXHKUS)

funding.label: Funding model & farebox recovery
funding.description: Share of operating costs covered by fares, where an official or agency-derived figure exists. Each system defines the ratio differently; figures are directional.

nyc.measure: MTA farebox operating ratio, all agencies, full-year 2025
nyc.ownership: Public: the MTA, a New York State public-benefit corporation
nyc.model: Fares and tolls covered 39% of the MTA operating budget in 2024, down from an average of 52% in 2012-2019, per the State Comptroller. The rest comes from dedicated taxes and state and city subsidies.
nyc.source: MTA Finance Committee financial performance report (Jan. 2026)

london.ownership: Public: Transport for London, part of the Greater London Authority
london.model: TfL reported passenger income of £5,004.4m in 2024/25. The rest of its income comes from grants, business rates, the congestion charge, advertising and property.
london.private: Bus routes are run by private operators under TfL contracts.

paris.measure: Fare revenue ÷ operating spending (our calculation from IDFM accounts)
paris.ownership: Public: Île-de-France Mobilités (IDFM), the regional authority; RATP and SNCF operate under contract
paris.model: In 2024 IDFM took in €4.3B in fare revenue and €6.4B in tax revenue, which includes the versement mobilité payroll tax on employers, against €11.5B in operating spending.
paris.private: Services are being opened to competitive tendering, starting with buses.

tokyo.ownership: Mixed: Tokyo Metro (listed Oct. 23, 2024) and Toei (Tokyo Metropolitan Government), plus JR East and private railways
tokyo.model: Tokyo Metro reported operating revenue of ¥422.4B and operating profit of ¥89.6B (21.2% margin) for the year to March 2026. Those totals include non-fare businesses.
tokyo.private: JR East and private railways run most commuter rail.
tokyo.source: Tokyo Metro earnings release, FY to March 2026

seoul.measure: Seoul Metro cost recovery per passenger (원가보전율)
seoul.ownership: Public: Seoul Metro (Seoul Metropolitan Government) and Korail
seoul.model: In 2025 Seoul Metro spent ₩1,817 per passenger against an average fare of ₩1,036. Cost recovery was 53.9% in 2024. The city covers the shortfall.
seoul.private: Some lines run as public-private concessions.
seoul.source: Herald Business, reporting Seoul Metro figures (June 2026)

beijing.model: We found no published farebox ratio. Fares have not changed since Dec. 2014.

shanghai.measure: Fares as share of pricing cost (Shanghai fare-hearing documents)
shanghai.model: Fare-hearing documents published in Aug. 2026 put fare coverage of pricing cost at about 55% for 2023-2025, the basis for a proposed fare revision.
shanghai.source: Yicai, on the Shanghai Development and Reform Commission hearing (Aug. 2026)

hongkong.measure: MTR does not publish a farebox ratio
hongkong.ownership: Mixed: MTR Corporation, listed in Hong Kong and majority-owned by the government
hongkong.model: MTR's 2024 net profit was HK$15.77B, of which HK$10.27B came from property development, the 'Rail plus Property' model. MIT's Transit Lab cites a 187% farebox ratio for 2015.
hongkong.private: Listed company with private minority shareholders.
